ai.title: 🤖 *AI Integration — Complete Explanation*
ai.intro: This bot is *powered by a real AI engine* — the same one that runs behind ChatGPT. When you ask something the bot doesn't have a canned reply for, it forwards your message to an AI server running on this machine that communicates with ChatGPT to generate a smart, human-like response.
ai.architecture:
Here is how the bot and AI server connect step-by-step:

```
  You (Telegram User)
        │
        ▼  sends message
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │  Telegram Bot    │  ← bot.js running on Node.js
  │  (mybot/bot.js)  │
  └──────┬───────────┘
         │ 1. NLU classifies intent
         │ 2. If no canned reply → send to AI
         ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │  AI Service      │  ← aiService.js
  │  (aiService.js)  │  spawns child process
  └──────┬───────────┘
         │ spawns node server.mjs on PORT 3001
         ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  ChatGPT Unofficial API Server   │  ← server.mjs
  │  /chatgpt-unofficial-api/client/ │
  │  Listens on: http://localhost:3001│
  └──────────┬───────────────────────┘
             │ uses cookies.json auth
             ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │  ChatGPT (OpenAI)            │
  │  — Generates the actual      │
  │    intelligent response      │
  └──────────────────────────────┘
             │
             ▼  response flows back up
         You see the reply in Telegram!
```

📌 **Key Point:** The ChatGPT Unofficial API is a reverse-engineered client that lets us talk to ChatGPT without an official API key. It runs as a *separate server* on port 3001, and the Telegram bot spawns it as a child process when the bot starts.
ai.how_it_works:
🔧 *How It Works (Step by Step)*

**Step 1:** You send a message to the Telegram bot.

**Step 2:** The bot's NLU (Natural Language Understanding) engine analyzes your message to figure out what you want:
   * Greeting? → responds with a hello
   * Asking for weather? → checks weather API
   * Asking a technical question? → forwards to AI
   * Telling a joke? → tells a joke from its library

**Step 3:** If your message doesn't match any predefined pattern (like a complex question about programming, Yihune's portfolio, or general knowledge), the bot sends your message to the AI server at `http://localhost:3001`.

**Step 4:** The AI server (`server.mjs`) connects to ChatGPT using the unofficial client (`index.mjs`), sends your message along with a special system prompt that tells the AI how to behave (Yihune's assistant style), and waits for a response.

**Step 5:** The AI-generated response comes back to the bot, which forwards it to you on Telegram. The bot also *remembers* this conversation in its memory system, so follow-up questions have context!
ai.tech_stack:
🛠 *Technology Stack — What's Under the Hood*

**📁 Project Structure:**
```
fullbot/
├── mybot/                          ← The Telegram Bot
│   ├── bot.js                      ← Entry point
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── services/
│   │   │   ├── aiService.js        ← Spawns & manages AI server
│   │   │   ├── memoryService.js    ← Conversation memory
│   │   │   ├── nluService.js       ← Intent classification
│   │   │   └── ...
│   │   ├── handlers/
│   │   │   ├── commandHandler.js   ← /ai, /help, etc.
│   │   │   ├── callbackHandler.js  ← Button clicks
│   │   │   └── messageHandler.js   ← Incoming messages
│   │   └── i18n/                   ← Translations
│   └── package.json
│
├── chatgpt-unofficial-api/         ← The AI Engine
│   └── client/
│       ├── server.mjs              ← HTTP server (port 3001)
│       ├── index.mjs               ← ChatGPT client
│       ├── cookies.json            ← Auth cookies
│       └── package.json
```

**🧩 Key Technologies:**
• **Node.js** — Runtime for both the bot AND the AI server
• **ChatGPT Unofficial API** — Reverse-engineered ChatGPT client (no official API key needed)
• **Port 3000** — where the Telegram bot's own HTTP server listens
• **Port 3001** — where the ChatGPT API proxy server listens
• **Child Process (spawn)** — aiService.js uses Node's `spawn()` to launch `server.mjs` as a separate process
• **Memory System** — Tracks the last 10 messages per user for conversation context
• **NLU Classifier** — Trained on 10 intents to understand what you want
• **i18n** — Full bilingual support (English + Afaan Oromoo)
ai.capabilities:
✨ *What the AI Can Do For You*

Here are some *real examples* of what you can ask the AI:

**💻 Programming & Technical Questions**
> "How do I create a REST API with Node.js and Express?"
> "What's the difference between React and React Native?"
> "Explain async/await in JavaScript with an example"
> "How do I connect MongoDB to my Node.js app?"

**👤 Questions About Yihune Belay**
> "What technologies does Yihune work with?"
> "Tell me about Yihune's portfolio"
> "What projects has Yihune built?"
> "Can Yihune help me with my app idea?"

**💬 General Conversation (with memory!)**
> User: "What's the capital of France?"
> Bot: "The capital of France is Paris."
> User: "What's the weather like there?"
> Bot: "I told you about Paris — let me check the weather for you!"

**🧠 Contextual Memory**
The bot remembers our conversation! For example:
> "My name is John"
> "Nice to meet you, John!"
> (10 messages later)
> "What's my name?"
> "Your name is John 😊"

**❌ When AI is Unavailable**
If the AI server fails to start or crashes, the bot gracefully falls back to canned replies (pre-written responses) so you still get an answer — just not as smart.
ai.commands:
📋 *AI-Related Commands (What You Can Type)*

**👤 For Everyone (Users)**
• **`/ai`** — Show this full AI explanation with architecture and examples
• **`/ai status`** — Check if the AI server is running right now
• **`/ai model`** — See which AI model is active
• **`/ai help`** — Same as /ai, shows detailed info

**🔐 For Admin Only**
• **`/ai restart`** — Restart the AI server if it crashed or is stuck
• **`/ai model gpt-4`** — Switch to a different AI model (example: gpt-4, gpt-3.5, auto)

**💡 Pro Tip:** You don't even need to use these commands! Just talk to the bot naturally. If your question is complex, the AI will handle it automatically in the background. The commands are only if you're curious about *how* it works or want to check its status.
ai.troubleshooting:
🔍 *Troubleshooting — When AI Doesn't Work*

**Symptom: Bot gives boring/robotic replies**
→ The AI server might be down. Type `/ai status` to check.
→ If stopped, ask the admin to type `/ai restart`.

**Symptom: "AI server process error" in logs**
→ This means the ChatGPT API server couldn't start.
→ Check that Node.js is installed at `/usr/bin/node`.
→ Make sure `cookies.json` exists in `/chatgpt-unofficial-api/client/`.

**Symptom: Port 3001 already in use**
→ Another process is hogging the port. Kill it with:
   `kill -9 $(lsof -ti:3001)`

**Symptom: AI response is too slow (>30s)**
→ ChatGPT's free tier can be rate-limited. Wait a moment and try again.
→ Or ask the admin to restart the AI server.
ai.tips:
💡 *Tips for Best Results*

✅ **Be specific** — Instead of "tell me something", ask "How do I build a login page with React?"
✅ **Ask follow-ups** — The AI remembers our conversation, so you can dig deeper
✅ **Be patient** — The AI needs a few seconds to think and generate a response
✅ **Use /forget** — If you want to start a completely new topic without context, use /forget to clear memory
✅ **Use natural language** — Talk to the bot like you would talk to a person, not a search engine
✅ **Check /ai status** — If responses seem weird, check if the AI server is running
